1: Om. This syllable is all of this. Here is its explanation. What has been, what is, and what will be: all of it is Om. Whatever else lies beyond the three times, that too is Om.
2: All of this is Brahman. This Self is Brahman. This Self has four quarters.
3: The first quarter is Vaishvanara. Its place is waking. It knows what is outside. It has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and it takes in the solid world.
4: The second quarter is Taijasa. Its place is dream. It knows what is inside. It has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and it takes in the subtle world.
5: When a sleeper wants nothing and sees no dream, that is deep sleep. The third quarter is Prajna. Its place is deep sleep. In it everything has become one, a single mass of knowing. It is made of bliss and takes in bliss, and awareness is its door.
6: This is the lord of all. This knows all. This is the ruler within. This is where everything comes from, for beings arise from it and return to it.
7: Not turned inward, not turned outward, not both ways at once, not a mass of knowing, not knowing, not unknowing. It cannot be seen, used, grasped or marked. It cannot be thought or named. Its substance is the one steady sense of self. In it the world falls quiet. It is peace, it is good, it is one without a second. This they call the fourth. That is the Self. That is what is to be known.
8: This Self, taken as a syllable, is Om. Taken as sounds, the quarters are the sounds and the sounds are the quarters: a, u and m.
9: Vaishvanara, whose place is waking, is a, the first sound, because it runs through everything and because it comes first. One who knows this gains what they wish for and becomes first.
10: Taijasa, whose place is dream, is u, the second sound, because it is higher and because it stands between the two. One who knows this carries knowledge forward and is even with everyone. No one in their family is born without knowing Brahman.
11: Prajna, whose place is deep sleep, is m, the third sound, because it measures and because everything merges into it. One who knows this measures all of this and becomes the place where it merges.
12: The fourth has no sound. It cannot be used or handled. In it the world falls quiet. It is good and one without a second. So Om is the Self itself. One who knows this goes into the Self by the Self.
